stated: The Conservative Party will continue support for leaseholders affected by historic building safety problems by requiring the continuation of developer-funded remediation programmes for mid- and high-rise buildings.

source.quote: After delivering landmark new laws that freed leaseholders from cladding bills following on from the awful tragedy of Grenfell Tower, we will continue our support for leaseholders affected by historic building safety problems by requiring the continuation of developer-funded remediation programmes for mid- and high-rise buildings.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly addresses building fire-safety risk (cladding remediation post-Grenfell), materially affecting residents' physical safety in mid- and high-rise homes.

The cladding crisis has left leaseholders trapped in unmortgageable, unsellable properties; developer-funded remediation restores tenure security and property marketability, bearing directly on housing affordability for affected households.

Without developer liability, leaseholders face remediation bills of tens-to-hundreds of thousands of pounds plus interim-safety service-charge surges (waking watches etc.), directly destroying disposable income and ability to afford essential housing bills; continuing the programme shields them from these costs.

membership_note: The policy's primary effects are on housing security/marketability (O1) and the direct cost burden on leaseholders (O2). A building-safety/fire-risk dimension exists but does not map cleanly to O5's defined indicators (crime, policing, national security). O12 and O13 tradeoffs (developer liability chilling future supply, public-finance savings vs. developer-sector drag) are plausible but too speculative and marginal relative to the existing programme to clear the non-negligible bar here.
